paper_metadata.title: Response to “Exponential challenges in unbiasing quantum Monte Carlo algorithms with quantum computers”

summary: This response paper studies QC-GFMC overlap estimation on the 1D transverse-field Ising model, reporting numerical results for Γ/J = 0.5 with L = 6 to 12 and for Γ/J = 1.0 with L = 12. It finds that a trial wavefunction with λ = 0.127 reproduces the exact ground-state energy to better than 99.8% for L = 6–12, and that sophisticated walkers can sharpen overlap distributions and reduce local-energy variance, but no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Numerical study of QC-GFMC on the 1D transverse-field Ising model at Γ/J = 0.5, using a sophisticated trial wavefunction and comparing overlap/local-energy statistics versus measurement count and system size.

hyperparameters.walker_type: non-orthogonal states generated by 1,2,...,L spin flips from |Ψ_MC⟩

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Trial wavefunction parameter λ set to 0.127; walkers constructed from spin-flip excitations of |Ψ_MC⟩

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum Monte Carlo overlap estimation between trial and walker wavefunctions for a spin model; no explicit qubit encoding described in this response paper
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate overlaps ⟨Ψ_T|φ⟩ and local energies for QC-GFMC on the 1D TFIM
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = -J Σ_k σ^z_k σ^z_{k+1} - Γ Σ_k σ^x_k

problem_instance.description: 1D transverse-field Ising model with periodic boundary conditions

dataset_specification.description: Periodic boundary conditions; Γ/J = 0.5; system sizes L = 6 to 12

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 16 independent simulations for overlap/local-energy plots; GFMC results averaged over 128 independent runs; measurement-count scaling studied as a function of M

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute overlap distributions and local energies; compare energy-per-site error versus M^{-1/2}

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: weak system-size dependence of total energy with number of samples

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report a classical baseline or a quantified speedup for this experiment; it only states that QC-GFMC may be useful in this regime and that exponential measurement overhead is not necessarily the bottleneck for finite-size problems.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Measurement overhead for overlap estimation can grow exponentially with system size in general

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Quantum overlap estimation for QC-GFMC; paper discusses up to 16 qubits in prior work and presents numerical simulations, but no hardware resource accounting for this response paper.
limiting_factors: No explicit quantum hardware run reported in this response paper
Measurement overhead can grow exponentially with system size
Results are numerical studies of overlap/local-energy behavior, not a full end-to-end advantage demonstration

notes: This is a response paper about QC-QMC numerics; it reports no specific quantum hardware, qubit count, or circuit depth for the presented TFIM/GFMC simulations.

The experiment is gate-based in the broader thesis sense only insofar as it discusses quantum computers for overlap estimation, but the paper does not specify an executable gate circuit or hardware run.
The paper argues QC-QMC may remain promising and shows weak system-size dependence for Γ/J = 0.5, but it does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.
